name: WebRTC local IP discovery
plain: Uses a WebRTC peer connection to learn the device's local and public IP addresses.
meaning: Can reveal a real IP behind a VPN and LAN addresses. Browsers now often hide local addresses behind mDNS names. LinkedIn uses stun.l.google.com:19302 and an IP regex.

chrome.note: Local IPs masked by mDNS since about Chrome 75

limits.headline: Can try to learn your device's home network address and public address through a call setup
limits.user_action: Nothing. A page can start a call setup without a pop up
can: Ask an outside server for your public address
See a masked .local name for your home network address in most browsers
See your real home network address if you allowed camera or microphone
Compare addresses to spot a VPN
cannot: See your real home network address by default in modern browsers
Beat a VPN that carries call traffic too
See other devices on your network from this alone
Work without a script running on the page
limits.reach_label: Mostly hidden, can leak a VPN

story.what_it_is: A page can use a call feature to learn your device's home network address and public address.

marketing.name: RTCPeerConnection
marketing.pitch: The call building block that gathers network paths so two browsers can connect directly.

story.for_you: You never see it. A page can quietly start a call setup and read the addresses it finds. Modern browsers hide the home address behind a random name, but the public one may still show.
story.for_makers: Makers need these addresses to connect calls and games directly. Tracking and fraud scripts also read them to see past some VPNs. Privacy settings can block this, but may break calls.

use_cases.example: Browser video calls such as Google Meet gather addresses so your computer and the other person's can connect directly.
A browser multiplayer game with peer to peer links finds addresses of all players so they can connect without a central relay.
A cloud gaming page builds a live video path to the game server using the paths found by this feature.
A fraud tool reads the public address found by the call setup to see if it differs from the page request address, which may show a VPN.
A tracking script reads the addresses to tell devices apart, a trick browsers now limit.
A web voice chat joins a room and shares your path with friends so audio stays low delay.
A developer uses a leak test page to check what a site can learn through calls.

technical_bounds: mDNS hides host addresses by default
STUN request also leaks the public IP to Google

linkedin.how: Collector key(s): webrtc. STUN stun.l.google.com:19302 and IP regex.
